I find this to be very interesting. The concept of prisoners marrying one another had never crossed my mind before. It awakens a conflict of emotion -- on one hand I wish them the very best yet I wonder are they together for love or simple companionship to ease the difficulty of prison and to have a sense of normalcy, connection and control in their lives in an otherwise regimented life? Does that detract from the relationship/marriage? I would think not, in my opinion. It's a valid and human response, if so and hopefully they can find solace in one another.

Then the other hand chimes in -- but these are murderers. They killed people and ended their lives. They are there for punishment. Ah, yes, but they are also human beings with needs of their own and through love comes growth. And even if they were not to change their fundamental interior character (that of unrepentant murderer, perhaps) should they not still be allowed to seek out human connections while serving their court appointed punishments?

Well . . . I suppose I should stop carrying this debate on with my hands.
